findings.title: Ledger Investigates CryptoBilis Reseller Channel After Crypto Loss Reports
findings.summary_md: TokenPost reported that Ledger was investigating reported cryptocurrency losses linked to devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, with estimated transfers exceeding $86 million across Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron. Ledger asked CryptoBilis to pause sales and shipments while the investigation continued, and customers who bought devices within the past 90 days were advised not to initialize unused devices. Ledger had not confirmed a compromise of its devices, firmware or broader infrastructure, and the investigation was focused on the reseller channel serving Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.

findings.title: Hidden implant in Ledger hardware wallets linked to $93M theft
findings.summary_md: Help Net Security reported that an unauthorized hardware implant in Ledger wallets sold through CryptoBilis was linked to roughly $93 million in thefts. The implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the device screen during setup, decodes it via an onboard microcontroller, and exfiltrates it over LTE. Ledger confirmed that all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident involved devices sold through CryptoBilis.

findings.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported that Ledger confirmed some devices distributed through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were compromised with a hardware implant that drained users' cryptocurrency wallets. The implant is a physical supply-chain modification inside the enclosure that intercepts screen output. Ledger asked resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to halt sales until the investigation concluded.

findings.title: Trezor Removes CryptoBilis From Reseller List Amid Device Review
findings.summary_md: TokenPost reported that Trezor removed CryptoBilis from its reseller list and stopped selling products through the company as a precaution while reviewing concerns about devices sold by the reseller. At that time Trezor said there was no indication its devices were affected and no reports of tampering had been received. The move followed broader concerns involving the Southeast Asian reseller, including an earlier investigation into the CryptoBilis channel linked to reported cryptocurrency losses.

findings.title: CryptoBilis update
findings.summary_md: Trezor posted on X that it learned through responsible disclosure of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 bought from reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026. The device was purchased via Tokopedia and the implant appears to operate similarly to those seen in Ledger devices. Trezor said no funds have been reported stolen and urged CryptoBilis buyers from March 2026 onward to move funds to a new wallet with a new seed.

findings.title: Trezor warns of suspected hardware implant in CryptoBilis wallet
findings.summary_md: Crypto.news reported that Trezor warned customers who bought devices from reseller CryptoBilis to move their funds after a suspected hardware implant was reported in a Safe 5 wallet purchased in August 2026. The implant was described as an extra circuit board between the main board and screen with a cellular module and antenna. CryptoBilis was removed as an authorized Trezor reseller on October 9 after Ledger confirmed tampered hardware wallets sold through the same reseller.

findings.title: Trezor Treats One Report of an Implanted CryptoBilis Safe 5 as Credible Before Examining It
findings.summary_md: Yahoo reported that Trezor treated a single report of an implanted Safe 5 from CryptoBilis as credible before examining the device and credited SEAL 911 for help with the response. The company removed CryptoBilis as a reseller on October 9 following reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through it. An onchain analyst tallied more than $86 million drained from Ledger users across the related CryptoBilis incident.

findings.title: Trezor Warns CryptoBilis Buyers After Report of Hardware Implant in Safe 5
findings.summary_md: Decrypt reported that Trezor was made aware through responsible disclosure of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 bought from CryptoBilis in August 2026. The implant sits between the main board and screen and appears capable of reading the recovery phrase from the screen and transmitting it over a mobile network when plugged in. Trezor advised affected buyers to move funds to a new wallet with a new seed and offered replacement devices or vouchers for purchases since March 2026.

findings.title: Trezor Warns of Suspected Hardware Implant in One of Its Wallets Sold by CryptoBilis
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that Trezor warned CryptoBilis buyers to replace wallet recovery phrases after a customer reported a Safe 5 implant that transmits them over cellular. The implant includes an extra circuit board with a cellular module and antenna fitted between the main board and screen. Trezor has not independently verified the device and no affected customers have reported fund losses so far.
